source.title: Shaping the learning landscape in neural networks around wide flat minima
source.authors: Carlo Baldassi; Fabrizio Pittorino; R. Zecchina

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares trained networks’ loss-landscape properties with generalization performance using local entropy and Hessian spectra, a conceptual test of whether measured network properties track generalization.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports results on random patterns and randomized Fashion-MNIST, but those do not test the listed versions: random patterns have no generalization, and randomized Fashion-MNIST is used for volume, Hessian, and noise-robustness comparisons.
record.test_reason: The study measures local entropy and Hessian curvature against test error in committee machines. These results concern a related construct, but do not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure in convolutional networks or any other listed version. Randomizing input pixels is not a fixed-random-label experiment.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the real-data findings. The broader conclusion is that wide flat minima exist in the studied continuous-weight nonconvex models, cross-entropy favors such regions, and entropy-driven algorithms or controlled weight-norm schedules can find them. The Fashion-MNIST experiments suggest a connection to generalization; extension to deeper networks remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses committee machines, local-entropy volume estimates and Hessian spectra; it does not reproduce the listed versions’ interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that slowing the growth of weight norms in ceSGD changes the quality of minima reached; on randomized Fashion-MNIST, eLAL is slightly worse than ceSGD in local volumes at short distances.

fits_no_version.finding: Across four training procedures and 50 runs per procedure, zero-training-error committee machines on 500 filtered, binarized Dress/Coat Fashion-MNIST examples show an association between lower maximum Hessian eigenvalue, wider minima, and lower test error. Figure 7 reports the association graphically.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this normalized committee-machine setting, wider minima and lower curvature of smoothed MSE tend to accompany better generalization.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
record.problems: The real-data experiment uses a small two-class subset and a fully-connected committee machine; fBP could not be run on that data. Figure 7 reports the test-error relationship graphically without numeric values or uncertainty estimates for the plotted points.
record.rows_left_out: No other result rows meet the version-specific row criteria. Random-pattern experiments do not measure generalization; randomized Fashion-MNIST results concern local volume, Hessian spectra, and input-noise robustness rather than a listed version.

untested.parts: No matched natural-label versus fixed-random-label experiment reporting training fit and held-out accuracy. Appendix F shuffles inputs and does not measure held-out accuracy on the randomized data.
No test-error sweep over widths beyond the width required for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.

No magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness measurement in a convolutional family, or ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Controlling weight norms does not make maximum Hessian eigenvalue the specified measure.
No removal of memorized training examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: T6 is relative to the listed versions; the paper does conduct its own experiments on generalization. The rows' version links are correct, but the record's study-level tests/T2 classification is not.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of fitting random labels and natural labels using the same architecture and training recipe.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

The study relates local entropy and maximum Hessian eigenvalue to generalization, but does not measure magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness or compare it with norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal or retraining of memorized examples.

rows.subject: fully-connected committee machine, LAL
rows.operation_detail: Compared test error with maximum eigenvalue of the Hessian spectrum.
rows.measure: Test error versus maximum Hessian eigenvalue; figure shows the relationship without numeric values in text.
rows.note: The figure caption says maximum eigenvalue is correlated to generalization; this is not the magnitude-aware perturbation measure specified in V7.
rows.check: The Hessian/test-error association is reported, but cannot establish any listed version. The Hessian is computed on smoothed MSE with tanh activations at beta = 90, with normalized weights.
